items.title: 68191_William (Bill) H. Challis Oral History Interview
items.q: Ferde and I were three, you know, we were the arranging staff at one time.

ctx.x: Yet, Whiteman had the title, the King of Jazz.

Well, I think he was the King of Jazz all right. That was the Jazz Era with Benny, you know, he was King of Swing. Anyway, let's see, we come back and we made a few records, Old Man River and something -- another thing I must say, first, Ferde he was wonderful to me, he took me in. After all I was a real know-nothing, you might say, and there's a guy that had symphony experience and music. He knew what he was doing and for years, he knew what he was doing; but he was awfully nice to me, and he gave me nice tunes…

Very often, I was in the -- I did some work in the show business actually, for theatres and you get four or five arrangers, and also I did it around the studios, I had the experience, of the guys wanting to pick out tunes. They're around with the leader and they want to grab this tune and grab that tune. It was dog eat dog sort of thing, and with Ferdie, he comes up with Old Man River and he comes up with several other tunes, and they were all nice, but I never had this
